wins: Mapped initial external attack surface, identifying SSH (22) and HTTP (80) services with accurate banner collection (ep001_step03).
Executed targeted HTTP enumeration, revealing multiple directories and a potential upload endpoint for later exploitation (ep001_step07).
fails: Failed to achieve persistence due to inability to escalate from limited web user to administrative context (ep001_step20).
Repeated attempts to deploy web-shell payloads were blocked by WAF responses, preventing command execution (ep001_step18).
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance phase is solid, but lack of privilege escalation and reliable payload delivery blocked goal completion.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts stalled because no local exploit matched the detected kernel version; brute-force scripts timed out.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner indicates OpenSSH 8.x
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with nmap scripts

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP responds with 200 and directory listing reveals upload form
skill_cards.then_action: Automate upload testing with Burp Intruder and verify file execution

memory_ops.reason: High consistency in initial SSH reconnaissance leading to accurate service profiling.
Upload form enumeration repeatedly revealed actionable endpoints worth revisiting.

next_experiments.title: Experiment: Privilege escalation chaining
next_experiments.description: After downloading system info, match kernel build to known exploits (searchsploit) and test locally patched binaries to escalate from web user.

next_experiments.title: Experiment: WAF-aware payload delivery
next_experiments.description: Use Burp to fuzz upload parameters with smaller chunks and non-standard encodings to bypass WAF blocking and reach command execution.

next_experiments.title: Experiment: SSH key harvesting
next_experiments.description: If hidden SSH keys are detected in upload directories, attempt to use them for lateral movement with ssh -i.
